metaDescription: Four storm-ready generators compared on running watts, dual fuel, transfer switch readiness and tank life, plus a pre-storm fuel and placement plan.
expertTake: The Westinghouse 12500 dual fuel is the pick for most storm-prone homes because it pairs a 9,500-watt running rating with propane flexibility and a 30A transfer-switch outlet. The Oxseryn 4400 is the value pick for a refrigerator, lights and fans only, and anyone who will not buy fuel and a transfer setup before the storm should skip the generator and plan around a battery station.
introParagraphs: Hurricane season changes the generator question from convenience to endurance. The real test is not a four-hour blackout but a week without grid power, when fuel supply, runtime per tank and how the machine connects to the house decide whether you stay comfortable.

Storm buyers also face a timing trap: shelves empty out within days of a forecast, and a generator bought in a rush often arrives with no fuel plan and no safe place to run it. These picks are judged on what keeps a household going through a long outage, not on camping-weekend specs.

products.name: Westinghouse 12500W Dual Fuel Home Backup Generator
products.description:
A 9,500-watt running rating on gasoline is enough to run a refrigerator, a chest freezer, a sump pump, a window air conditioner, lights and a router on the same circuit set. What makes this Westinghouse a hurricane pick rather than a jobsite pick is the propane mode: 8,500 running watts on LPG means you can burn through a stack of cylinders that stored without degrading, instead of depending on gasoline that goes stale in a garage.

The outlet layout leans toward home backup, with a 30A transfer-switch-ready receptacle alongside the household and RV outlets, so a licensed electrician can wire an inlet and let you power chosen circuits without extension cords through a window. The 457cc engine uses a cast iron sleeve, which is the right material for long running hours. Against the DuroStar, it gives up a few hundred running watts on paper but is the better documented of the two.

Ownership is about preparation. Before the season, run it under load, confirm the propane hose seals, and keep fresh stabilized gasoline in approved cans. Top the oil up at every refill, because a big crankcase that runs for days still drinks it, and an extended outage is the wrong moment to discover the oil is a quart low.
products.bestFor: Households that want whole-circuit backup with a propane reserve for multi-day outages.
pros: 9,500 running watts covers fridge, freezer and pumps
30A transfer-switch outlet for a clean home hookup
Cast iron sleeve engine for long running hours
cons: A large, heavy machine that needs a safe outdoor spot
Running output falls on propane compared with gasoline

products.name: Westinghouse 14500W Dual Fuel Home Backup Generator
products.description:
Westinghouse built this one around automation. Paired with its WATS200 automatic transfer switch, it can start itself and take over the house when the grid drops, which is the only way to get coverage while you are evacuating a family member or are away from home. That single feature separates it from every other pick here, because an outage that starts at 3 a.m. should not require you to be awake.

The 550cc engine uses a pressure lubrication system, which pushes oil to the bearings instead of relying on splash alone, a design advantage for a machine that might run around the clock for days. Copper windings and under 5 percent THD keep power clean enough for phones, computers and televisions, though the figure is looser than the sub-3 percent claims on inverter models. It is also the largest machine here, so confirm your electrician is comfortable with the transfer setup before the season.

The tradeoff is cost, weight and the need for professional installation. If you only want to plug in a fridge and a fan, the 12500 or the Oxseryn gives you the practical result with less work. Test the automatic setup at the start of the season with the main breaker off, and keep the battery on a maintainer so the electric start is ready when the storm arrives.
products.bestFor: Homes that need automatic switchover and have budget for an installed transfer switch.
pros: Pairs with an automatic transfer switch for hands-off backup
Clean power for phones and televisions
Dual fuel provides a fuel fallback
cons: Needs a professionally installed transfer setup to use its best feature
Largest and heaviest option in the lineup

products.name: DuroStar DS13000MX 13,000W Dual Fuel Generator
products.description:
The DuroStar targets the same buyer as the Westinghouse 12500 with a 13,000-watt headline, a 500cc engine and remote start. Its carbon monoxide alert is worth a sentence of its own: it detects dangerous buildup and shuts the engine down automatically, which matters during a storm when people are tempted to move the generator closer to the house for shelter.

The listing gives a single output number and less breakdown between gasoline and propane than the Westinghouse, so treat the quoted 13,000 watts as a ceiling and ask for the running figure before you plan a load list. If it follows the usual ratio, running watts will sit well below the headline. That documentation gap is the main reason it ranks behind the Westinghouse pair here.

For ownership, plan on the same routine as any big open-frame set: change the oil after the first break-in hours, keep the air filter clean after wind-driven dust or salt air, and store a spare spark plug and a quart of the correct oil with your fuel cans. Coastal air is hard on terminals and fasteners, so a light coat of corrosion inhibitor on exposed hardware is cheap insurance.
products.bestFor: Buyers who want a large dual fuel unit with automatic CO shutdown and remote start.
pros: CO alert shuts the engine down automatically
Dual fuel gives a gasoline or propane choice
cons: Less detailed running-watt documentation than the Westinghouse
Heavy and noisy at full load compared with inverter models

products.name: Oxseryn 4400W Inverter Generator, RV Ready 30A
products.description:
When the goal is to keep a refrigerator, a few lights, a fan and phone chargers alive, 3,400 running watts is a sensible target and this Oxseryn delivers it from a two-gallon tank. Its ECO mode drops engine speed at light load, which is the single biggest factor in stretching a day's fuel when you are carrying jugs from a gas station that may have a line.

Despite the inverter label the frame is open, so it is noisier than an enclosed set and meant for outdoor use. The 30A RV outlet gives it a path to a transfer switch or an interlock setup with a proper cord, but the unit has no listed electric start or propane option, so every restart is a pull and every refill is gasoline. Against the Westinghouse 12500 it is far smaller, lighter and cheaper to feed.

Fuel is the whole ownership story. Use fresh gasoline with stabilizer, drain or run the carburetor dry before storage, and check the oil on each refill because the low-oil shutdown will stop the engine mid-night if it is low. The fourteen-hour figure applies to a quarter load, so expect fewer hours when a freezer, a fan and a few lights are all running together.
products.bestFor: Small households that only need refrigeration, lights, fans and device charging.
pros: ECO mode stretches fuel on light loads
30A RV outlet suits a transfer inlet
Low-oil and overload shutdown protect the engine
cons: Gasoline only, with recoil start on the listing
Not enough capacity for central air or a well pump plus a fridge

buyingCriteria.criterion: Plan for a week, not a night
buyingCriteria.explanation: A multi-day outage means refilling many times, so tank size and runtime at your real load matter more than headline watts. The Westinghouse 14500 and 12500 run on large tanks, while the Oxseryn 4400 holds only two gallons for roughly 14 hours at a quarter load. Multiply the refills you expect by the gasoline you can safely store, then decide.

A refrigerator, a sump pump and a few lights fit under 3,400 running watts, which the Oxseryn covers. Adding a well pump or a window air conditioner pushes you toward the 9,500 running watts of the Westinghouse 12500. Motor loads start at two to three times their running draw, so leave headroom.

Propane stores indefinitely while gasoline degrades in months, which is why dual fuel suits a stockpile bought before the season. The Westinghouse 12500 holds 8,500 running watts on propane versus 9,500 on gasoline. Natural gas hookups are not an option on these picks, so cylinders remain the only propane source.

Back-feeding a house through a dryer outlet is dangerous to utility workers and to you. A transfer switch or an interlock kit is the legal way, and the Westinghouse units list a 30A transfer-switch-ready outlet for it. The 14500 adds compatibility with an automatic transfer switch.

Most storm generator deaths come from carbon monoxide when units run in garages or too close to windows. Keep any generator outdoors, at least a generator-length of open space away from the house, and with exhaust pointing away from openings. The DuroStar's CO alert and shutdown is a helpful backstop, not a placement plan.

A generator must stay dry and upright. Use a generator-rated cover or a tent with open sides, raise the unit off standing water and chain it to a fixed object if looting or floodwater is a concern. Never run it under a closed shelter.

specDecoder.meaning: Running watts are what the engine can sustain for hours, peak covers a brief startup surge. Sizing a home load on peak numbers will overload the machine.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Westinghouse 12500 lists 12,500 peak but 9,500 running, so build your load list around 9,500.

specDecoder.meaning: Propane carries less energy per volume, so rated output drops on LPG. Check both ratings before assuming a load will carry over.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Westinghouse 12500 falls to 8,500 running watts on propane.

specDecoder.meaning: THD describes how clean the AC waveform is, and low numbers protect electronics. Inverter models usually quote under 3 percent while conventional sets run higher.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Westinghouse 14500 quotes under 5 percent THD, adequate for phones and TVs but looser than an inverter claim.

specDecoder.meaning: A fuel economy statement at quarter load, which is light. Real outage loads of a fridge plus a freezer plus fans typically run higher.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Oxseryn quotes up to 14 hours on two gallons, so expect fewer hours under a half load.

specDecoder.meaning: A dedicated outlet, usually a 30A or 50A twist lock, intended for a transfer switch or interlock inlet instead of loose extension cords.
specDecoder.watchFor: The Oxseryn has a 30A RV outlet but no explicit transfer-ready rating, so confirm with your electrician.

howWeEvaluated.title: Endurance over days
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed tank size, listed runtime and fuel flexibility because storm outages stretch for days. Dual fuel models earned credit for a stockable propane reserve. The Oxseryn's two-gallon tank scored lower for endurance.

howWeEvaluated.title: Home connection options
howWeEvaluated.description: We checked for transfer-switch-ready outlets and automatic switch compatibility, since a safe hookup is part of a storm kit. The Westinghouse 14500's WATS200 pairing was the strongest feature on this front. Units without a clear home-backup outlet lost points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity versus real loads
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared running watts to a typical outage load: a fridge, a freezer, a sump pump and a few lights. The 9,500-watt Westinghouse covers that and more, while the 3,400-watt Oxseryn covers only the basics. Ratings were read from the spec sheet, not from marketing peaks.

howWeEvaluated.title: Safety features
howWeEvaluated.description: CO shutdown, low-oil protection and overload shutdown were compared based on listing data. The DuroStar's CO alert is the only automatic CO feature stated in this lineup. No feature was treated as a substitute for outdoor placement.

howWeEvaluated.title: Ownership burden
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered weight, fuel storage needs and how easy each listing makes it to know what you are buying. The Westinghouse pair documents fuel-specific ratings clearly, while the DuroStar offers a single headline figure. Storm-season service access also factored in.

cards.label: Gasoline
cards.text: Gasoline delivers the highest output and is easy to find until a storm hits, then lines form. It stales in months, so stabilize it and rotate stock. The Oxseryn 4400 depends on gasoline entirely.

cards.label: Propane
cards.text: Propane cylinders can sit unused for years and burn cleanly, which fits a pre-season stockpile. The Westinghouse 12500 keeps 8,500 running watts on LPG and the DuroStar and 14500 are also dual fuel.

howToChoose.note: Choose dual fuel if you can store cylinders safely, and gasoline only if your needs are small and you will rotate fuel.

You want remote start from indoors
Few controls and a small footprint

howToChoose.subheading: For Refrigerators and Sump Pumps Specifically

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: Check the nameplate starting watts of the refrigerator and sump pump, since compressors and pumps surge two to three times their running draw. Size your running total at about 70 percent of the generator's rating, and check that the outlet type matches your cords.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Oxseryn 4400 handles a modern refrigerator and a small sump pump, while a freezer, a pump and an air conditioner together call for the Westinghouse 12500 with its 9,500 running watts.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You live where outages last a week or more, run medical equipment or a well pump, or want automatic backup while evacuated. The Westinghouse 12500 and 14500 justify the price in those cases.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You only need a fridge, lights and charging, and can ride out a few days with fewer comforts. The Oxseryn 4400 covers that with less fuel and less to store.

maintenance.why: Run the unit under load for 30 minutes to find stale fuel or a weak battery before it matters. A storm is the worst time to discover it will not start.

maintenance.interval: Before every start and every refill
maintenance.why: Low-oil shutdown stops the engine mid-outage. Big engines running continuously burn a little oil.
Gasoline loses volatility and gums jets. Rotate stabilized fuel into a car and buy fresh.
Electric and remote start depend on a charged battery. A trickle charger keeps the Westinghouse and DuroStar ready.
Salt air attacks terminals and fasteners. Wipe down and coat exposed hardware lightly.

faq.q: How many watts do I need to run a house in an outage?
faq.a: Essentials such as a refrigerator, lights and a router fit under 3,400 running watts. Adding a well pump, sump pump and window air conditioner moves you toward 7,000 to 9,500 running watts.

faq.q: Is propane better than gasoline for hurricane season?
faq.a: Propane stores for years and does not degrade, which suits a stockpile, but it lowers output by about ten percent. Gasoline gives full output but needs rotation and gets scarce after a storm warning.

faq.q: Can I run a generator in the garage with the door open?
faq.a: No. Carbon monoxide can still build up and enter the house. Run it outdoors, well away from windows, doors and vents.

faq.q: Do I need a transfer switch?
faq.a: If you only plug appliances into the generator, no. To power hardwired circuits safely you need a transfer switch or an interlock kit installed by a licensed electrician, which also prevents back-feeding the grid.

faq.q: Why do the peak and running ratings differ?
faq.a: Peak covers a few seconds of motor startup, while running watts are continuous. The Westinghouse 12500 lists 12,500 peak and 9,500 running, so use the lower number.

faq.q: When should I buy a generator for the season?
faq.a: Well before a storm forecast, because stock and fuel disappear within days. Buy early, test it, and store cylinders and stabilized fuel in advance.
